title: Check yourself: evidence, views and the log

blocks.text: Questions on what this page has just taught. Choose one answer for each.

questions.stem: A colleague reproduces a rejected 0200 from your log, which runs through ProtectedLogListener. They read its <isomsg> block with XMLPackager, set the iso87ascii packager, and put a test PIN block into field 52 because packing failed there. Field 2 in the block reads 555555______4444. What does pack() give now?

options.text: An ISOException at field 2, since a numeric field packager refuses the underscores
options.says: 17.2 (3): the numeric field packager doesn't check that a value is digits when it packs; the masked value packs without a word

options.text: An ISOException at field 2, since the masked value is shorter than the card number
options.says: 17.2: the mask keeps the length; 411111______1111 has the right length and packs

options.text: Bytes of the sent length that carry the underscores, since its field packager doesn't check what the value holds
options.says: 17.2 (3): the message packs to the original length with the masked PAN on the wire, a message nobody sent

options.text: Bytes of the sent length that carry the real card, since the mask only changes how the log displays it
options.says: 17.2: the block holds only the masked value; the real card is not in the log to come back

origin.section: 17.2 A Logged Message Gives Back the Bytes Only After You Put Back What the Log Masked

questions.stem: A client's logger has ProtectedLogListener first (protect 2 35 45), then a writer. For one day DebugFilter is added to the channel to chase a byte problem. What does that day's log show of the card number of each reply received?

options.text: Masked in the message and masked in the image, since the filter masks every entry of the event
options.says: 17.6: ProtectedLogListener masks only ISOMsg entries; DebugFilter's image is a Dumpable

options.text: Masked in the message and readable in the image, since the filter masks only the message entries
options.says: 17.4 and 17.6: the unpacked message is masked, and the image shows the card in its text column

options.text: Readable in the message and readable in the image, since the channel's filters run before the logger's
options.says: 17.4: the message in the same event is masked; the logger's filter sees the event after the channel built it

options.text: Readable in the message and absent from the image, since DebugFilter dumps only the header
options.says: 17.4: DebugFilter adds the header and the image, and the image holds the whole message

origin.section: 17.4 Each View of the Bytes Answers a Different Question

questions.stem: A service numbers the messages of its upstream link with an AtomicLong that is never reset or wrapped, and formats field 11 with ISOUtil.zeropad(n, 6), the long form. What goes out as message number 1,000,000?

options.text: A message with STAN 000000, since the long form keeps only the last six digits
options.says: 17.5: zeropad(long, len) keeps the last len digits and never complains

options.text: A message with STAN 100000, since the long form keeps only the first six digits
options.says: 17.5: the leading digit is the one that is lost

options.text: No message at all, since zeropad throws an ISOException for a seven-digit value
options.says: 17.5: only zeropad(String, len) throws; the long form cuts silently

options.text: No message at all, since the packager refuses a seven-digit field 11
options.says: 17.5: the value handed to the packager already has six digits, 000000

origin.section: 17.5 ISOUtil's Helpers Fail Quietly Where You Expect an Error

questions.stem: A logger has, in this order: ProtectedLogListener, FlatLogListener, a RealmLogFilter enabling host-channel and client.sender, and a writer. What does the writer write for a purchase logged under the realm client.sender?

options.text: Nothing, since the realm filter drops any event a filter before it has changed
options.says: 17.6.1: the realm filter looks only at the realm; with the order protect, realm filter, flat, the event is written

options.text: The event on one line with the card masked, since the mask is applied before the event is flattened
options.says: 17.6.1: the mask does come first, but the run with this order wrote nothing: the realm filter after the flattening keeps nothing

options.text: The event on one line with the card in clear, since the flat text is rendered from the original message
options.says: 17.6.1: flattening after the mask renders the masked copy; with this order the problem is the realm, not the mask

options.text: Nothing, since the event after flattening no longer carries a realm the filter can keep
options.says: 17.6.1: FlatLogListener passes a frozen event with no source, so the realm filter keeps nothing

origin.section: 17.6.1 Spot the Problem: One Line per Event

concepts: DebugFilter puts the image a channel read next to the unpacked message, and the image shows the card number unmasked.
FlatLogListener passes on a frozen text event with no message and no realm, so masking and realm filters must come before it.

A message read back from a protected log packs to the sent bytes only after its packager is set and every masked or wiped field gets a test value; a masked card number packs silently into different bytes.
zeropad(long) keeps the last digits silently, protect masks the whole track after the separator, and bitSet2String starts at bit 0.
